title: Practice 7: Running, swimming, climbing, crawling, dragging

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Том ___ (плавать — to swim, float, sail, there and back or in general) как топор.
exercises.why: **плавает** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **плавать** (to swim, to float) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **плыть** for one direction. present: я пла́ваю · ты пла́ваешь · он пла́вает · мы пла́ваем · вы пла́ваете · они пла́вают. — Wiktionary, «плавать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verb плавать — плыть, поплыть belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить — идти, пойти; "плавать" (like "ходить") is a "repeated function" verb. Note the ways in which it is used: Я умею плавать. — I know how to swim. Дерево плавает в воде. — Wood floats in water. Я плаваю на этом корабле. — I sail (work) on this ship. In naval terminology the verb "идти" instead of "плыть" is commonly used: Я иду на этом корабле. Наш корабль идёт по Чёрному морю. Мы шли в Архангельск.» — DLI, Lesson 73.  Compare: «Птицы летают, рыбы плавают, а собаки ходят.» (Birds fly, fish swim, and dogs walk.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Девочка любила ___ (лазать — to climb, there and back or in general) по деревьям.
exercises.why: **лазать** (the infinitive) (to climb, to clamber) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **лезть** for one direction. — Wiktionary, «лазать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite).» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «по деревьям» — movement in various directions, not towards one goal.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Они ___ (бежать — to run, one way) в сад, чтобы спастись от этих кровожадных собак.
exercises.why: **бежали** is the past tense (plural) of **бежать** ((imperfective only) to run, to be running) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **бегать** for many directions. past: он бежа́л · она бежа́ла · оно бежа́ло · они бежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «бежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs бегать-бежать, побежать belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить-идти, пойти. Note that in the conjugation of the verb "бежать", the consonants "ж" and "г" are alternated: я бегу, ты бежишь, они бегут. Note also that in all persons, except the 3rd person plural, it belongs to the 2nd conjugation: ты бежишь, он бежит, мы бежим, вы бежите. In the 3rd person plural it belongs to the 1st conjugation: они бегут.» — DLI, Lesson 82.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: They ran into the garden to save themselves from those blood-thirsty hounds.
exercises.context: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite).» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «часто» marks a repeated or habitual action, which is the job of the many-directions verb.  The other choice: **тащить** is from **тащить**, the one-direction verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.context: Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Наши собаки, пудель и такса, ___ (бегать — to run, there and back or in general) по двору.
exercises.why: **бегают** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **бегать** (to run) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **бежать** for one direction. present: я бе́гаю · ты бе́гаешь · он бе́гает · мы бе́гаем · вы бе́гаете · они бе́гают. — Wiktionary, «бегать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs бегать-бежать, побежать belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить-идти, пойти.» — DLI, Lesson 82.  «по двору» — movement in various directions, not towards one goal.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Я ___ (плавать — to swim, float, sail, there and back or in general) один-два раза в неделю.
exercises.why: **плаваю** is the present tense (1st person singular) of **плавать** (to swim, to float) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **плыть** for one direction. present: я пла́ваю · ты пла́ваешь · он пла́вает · мы пла́ваем · вы пла́ваете · они пла́вают. — Wiktionary, «плавать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verb плавать — плыть, поплыть belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить — идти, пойти; "плавать" (like "ходить") is a "repeated function" verb. Note the ways in which it is used: Я умею плавать. — I know how to swim. Дерево плавает в воде. — Wood floats in water. Я плаваю на этом корабле. — I sail (work) on this ship. In naval terminology the verb "идти" instead of "плыть" is commonly used: Я иду на этом корабле. Наш корабль идёт по Чёрному морю. Мы шли в Архангельск.» — DLI, Lesson 73.  Compare: «Птицы летают, рыбы плавают, а собаки ходят.» (Birds fly, fish swim, and dogs walk.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
